summary: Stone lookout on top of the Myles Standish Monument on Captain's Hill, Duxbury, MA; firetower.org says it operated from 1889 and was staffed until 1910. Monument is now a state park.

facts.design: Stone lookout on top of the 116-foot granite Myles Standish Monument
facts.status_note: The granite monument still stands as a state park; no source checked says what, if anything, of the lookout remains.

access.note: Myles Standish Monument State Reservation is a public recreation area; the monument's 125 steps can be climbed when it is open.

visit.trail_note: The park has walking trails and picnic tables.

events.note: firetower.org says first operated in 1889; the monument was not completed until 1898, so this date is unverified.
Commonwealth of Massachusetts began owning the monument and grounds.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register as US 26, MA 26 (September 3, 2008).

corrections.why: firetower.org gives the stone lookout as 116 ft (35.4 m), and Wikipedia gives the monument as 116 feet. The 70-foot figure in the 1919 State Forester report, quoted under January 1920, is for a steel tower that replaced the windmill tower at Chelmsford, not Duxbury.
The value is a date fragment from a quoted report, not an agency. firetower.org says the stone lookout was a municipal tower for the town of Duxbury.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org says the lookout first operated in 1889, but the monument it sat on was not completed until 1898. No source checked explains an 1889 operation, so the date is kept as unverified.
The January 1920 entry describes a windmill tower erected on the Myles Standish Reservation. It does not say it stood on Captain's Hill, so it is kept out of this record's events.

notes_for_editor: The 1889 start rests on one register entry, and the monument was not finished until 1898. The brief's height (21.3 m) and agency ('January 1920:') look like errors from the 1920 windmill-tower entry; corrected above. Brief elevation 54.9 m is not checked: Wikipedia says Captain's Hill is 200 ft (about 61 m) above sea level, but that may refer to the hilltop, not the record's point. A firelookout.org Duxbury listing turned up in search but returned 404 on fetch. Search also pointed to the Duxbury Rural & Historical Society (duxburyhistory.org) as a possible source for 1889 photographs; not checked. Read budget ran out before the 1920 windmill tower's exact site could be confirmed. Fact-check 2026-10-10: status changed from gone to unknown because no source checked says what remains. The 1920 windmill entry is not treated as this lookout, so the 1920 relocated event was removed from this file. The tower record data/towers/ma/us-ma-duxbury.json still reads status gone and was not edited.
